Léa Seydoux is getting an American Cinematheque retrospective celebrating her extensive filmography.
Over the course of two decades, Seydoux has built an acclaimed career in independent filmmaking (the Cannes Palme d’Or winner “Blue is the Warmest Color”) and major productions (Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune” movies and two James Bond films).
Seydoux’s American Cinematheque retrospective runs Thurs. Nov. 12-15 in Los Angeles, and features four of her films: Mia Hansen-Løve’s “One Fine Morning,” Abdellatif Kechiche’s “Blue is the Warmest Color,” Bertrand Bonello’s “The Beast” and Marie Kreutzer’s “Gentle Monster.” The French film star will appear for an in-person conversation about Netflix’s “Gentle Monster” with Kreutzer. In the harrowing film, Seydoux stars as a wife and mother reeling from the revelation her partner is involved in a ring producing child sex abuse materials. The story follows as Seydoux’s Lucy, a renowned pianist, confronts the complexities of love, trust and deception.
The American Cinematheque is a member-supported nonprofit cultural arts organization that has supported the movie-going experience since 1985. The Cinematheque showcases over 2,000 films per year and, last year, hosted a retrospective series for Oscar nominee Timothée Chalamet , as well as eventual best actor Oscar winner Michael B. Jordan.
Tickets for the screenings are now available on American Cinematheque’s website . The full schedule is below:
GENTLE MONSTER Q&A with filmmaker Marie Kreutzer and actor Léa Seydoux Fri. Nov. 13, 2026 | 7:30 p.m. Aero Theatre Free Members-Only Screening After moving to the countryside, Lucy hopes for a fresh start with her family — but a police visit and her husband’s dark secret shatter her world.
ONE FINE MORNING Thu. Nov. 12, 2026 | 7:00 p.m. Los Feliz 3
BLUE IS THE WARMEST COLOR Sat. Nov. 14, 2026 | 2:30 p.m. Egyptian Theatre
THE BEAST Sun. Nov. 15, 2026 | 9:30 p.m. Los Feliz 3
